ask/fast: Back to the bowl, f of x equals x squared. A bigger step size gets down faster: at zero point one, the ball crawls; at zero point four, it is there in a few hops.
ask/edge: But push it too far, and it breaks. At zero point nine five, x zigzags and settles. At one point zero five, barely more, every swing lands farther out.
ask/diverge: A walk that runs away like that, its swings growing without end, is said to diverge. So how big can a step be?
ask/name: In 1986, David Rumelhart, Geoffrey Hinton and Ronald Williams, who used steps like these to make programs learn, called the step size the learning rate.
ask/advice: Their advice: make it as large as possible without leading to oscillation, x swinging back and forth, since that learns fastest. On a bowl, the edges can be found exactly.
line/line: Each step multiplies x by one minus two A eta. Plot that factor against eta, with A at one: it falls from one in a straight line.
line/bands: Behind it are the walks it gives: sliding in above zero, zigzagging in down to minus one, and blowing up below.
line/half: It crosses zero at eta equals one over two A, a half here. A factor of zero leaves nothing of x: one step lands right on the minimum. Past that, x starts to swing.
line/edge: At eta equals one, it reaches minus one. Each step then flips x but keeps its size, so x bounces between two points forever. Any larger, and it diverges.
line/solve: Where is that edge for any A? Set the factor to minus one: one minus two A eta equals minus one.
line/solve2: Then two A eta must equal two.
line/max: Divide by two A: eta is one over A. That is the largest learning rate that does not diverge, written eta max.
line/widrow: Bernard Widrow and colleagues wrote down this same limit in 1976, for adaptive filters: circuits that tune their own settings by walking down a bowl.
line/steep: A steeper bowl, a bigger A, makes the line fall faster. With A at two, it reaches minus one at a half: steep walls need small steps.
slide/shift: Now slide the bowl so its bottom sits at three: f of x equals A times x minus three, squared.
slide/grad: Each slope is the old one at the same distance from the bottom, so the gradient is two A, times x minus three.
slide/dist: So each step multiplies the distance to the bottom by the same factor. With A at one and eta at zero point three, a ball at four is one away, and one step leaves it zero point four away.
slide/same: Sliding moves the minimum and nothing else: the factor, and so the limit of one over A, stay the same.
try/p1: Try one: f of x is four times x minus three, squared. What is the largest eta that does not diverge?
try/a1: Sliding changes nothing, so A is four, and the limit is one over four: zero point two five.
try/p2: Which eta lands on the minimum in one step?
try/a2: That needs a factor of zero: one over two A, which is one eighth, or zero point one two five.
try/p3: And with eta at zero point two, what does x do?
try/z1: The factor is one minus eight times zero point two: minus zero point six. That is between minus one and zero, so x zigzags in, closing on three.
